title: Never move a free feature behind the paywall
statement: Every paywall regression produced a lasting rating drop; pick the free tier once and hold it. Report 8: a competitor adding a paywall sent its users to a free rival, and free users explicitly warn against gating what is free. Report 10: soundscapes, longer timers, the event micropet and the anxiety breathing exercise all moved from free to paid; paywall-creep is the largest monetization theme (715). Report 11: an app whose third-largest praise theme was 'it's free' ('all functions are free', Dec 2025) retrofitted a paywall by Apr 2026 with no disclosure; five years without a sub-4★ review ended in three 1–2★ reviews in nine days.

title: Ratings follow the offer, not the feature set
statement: Trust (pricing, billing, support, delivering what was paid for) moves ratings more than features do.

title: Lead with a one-time lifetime purchase
statement: People buy because it is not a subscription; lifetime is the strongest pricing signal.

title: Price low and fair, anchored against subscription competitors
statement: 'Cheaper than a coffee' framing produces near-perfect ratings; know the price anchors users cite.

title: Know which competitors buyers compare against
statement: Buyers shop around before paying; competitor names and price anchors appear in reviews.

title: Stay minimal and ad-free
statement: Simple/clean is table stakes and the most praised trait; 'no ads' is the best-rated topic; every feature request comes with 'don't make it complicated'.

title: Generous fixed habit cap (or unlimited) — never change it
statement: A low or drifting free cap is the #1 monetization complaint; 'unlimited' also sells, so the level is a decision but the stability is not. Report 6: raising a 1-streak cap to 2 did not reduce complaints — the ask was unlimited — though the tone moved from 'scam' to 'love it, want more'. Report 7: a 4-habit cap held unchanged for 3½ years was still the top 2★ theme (0 of 27 complainers paid) while 11 users said 4 was plenty — stable is not enough if the level binds the 5–8-habit user. Report 11: 'First app that has more than 3 habits' was a reviewer's entire body — no cap was the acquisition wedge against the category, and whether it survived the paywall retrofit is unknown.

title: Daily check-in and one basic reminder per habit are free
statement: Core loop must be free; it draws no complaints when it is.

title: Basic widgets, icons and colours are free
statement: Loved, drives 5★, and re-paywalling widgets backfired. Report 7: with every widget Pro, the widget paywall was the only theme with zero 5★ reviews, while widgets were the best-loved feature; users proposed one free widget, more with Pro.

title: Backfill missed days / edit start date
statement: Users accept a bounded free backfill window. Report 8 contests it: a ~7-day backfill window in a free app with weak history views was the worst-rated request (mean 3.52).

title: Weekly / monthly / yearly reports
statement: The #1 stated reason people pay; under-counted by keywords, dominant in the qualitative read.

title: Week / month / year grid views
statement: 'Filling the squares' is the retention mechanic and emotional payoff.

title: Cloud sync / multi-device as the paid differentiator
statement: Strongest true differentiator among buyers (lift ×9.8). Report 7: absent for 3+ years, sync was the #1 3★/4★ theme with named willingness to pay; ship it opt-in and end-to-end (CloudKit private database) to keep a no-account privacy promise.

title: Multiple reminders per habit
statement: Moderate purchase reason; first reminder stays free.

title: Shared / group habits
statement: Strong purchase driver where it exists, but the worst-executed feature — demand is proven, execution is the risk.

title: Skip / holiday / pause mode (pause a habit or counter without losing history)
statement: Minor purchase factor; free or paid open. In report 3, pause/stop/archive is the highest-leverage missing feature (44 requests at mean 4.02, 'the only thing between me and 5★').

title: Passcode lock
statement: Minor; decide whether needed at all.

title: App-icon themes
statement: Minor purchase factor.

title: Quit-habit / bad-habit mode
statement: Well received where shipped; see Quit Habit Decision research doc.

title: Data export / backup / CSV
statement: Requested a lot from happy users, rarely a purchase trigger — charging for it generates requests, not revenue.

title: Apple Health integration
statement: Small volume, very high purchase intent.

title: Apple Watch app (done properly: timer, two-way sync)
statement: Small volume, very high purchase intent; a half-built Watch app draws 2–3★.

title: Interactive widget check-off
statement: Mark done without opening the app; small volume, very high intent.

title: Streaks / gamification
statement: High-priority praise, moderate purchase factor. Report 10 (contested): streaks added to a non-punitive pet app generated their own defect stream (171, growing 74×) and pressure stream (96) — net-negative in the written record for an ADHD audience.

title: Scholarship / hardship / discount program
statement: The cleanest 5★ generator in report 1 (91 of 101 mentions 5★); also works around broken payment rails; never switch it off. Report 10: a 'Guardian' pay-it-forward sponsorship programme is one of the only monetisation themes with a positive mean (4.76 across 708 mentions); its one complaint is that there is no visible way to apply.

title: Handle markets where card payment fails (RU, AR, TR, DZ, PK)
statement: Users who want to pay cannot; a discount/hardship path doubles as the workaround.

title: Localise early — it unlocks revenue
statement: Missing localisation is the biggest market-specific complaint and a stated purchase blocker; shipping a language visibly converts (Japan). Report 10: localisation is HIGH-PRIORITY at country level in eight storefronts at once (cn 26%, ru 18%, tr 19%, br 13%, es 12%); reviewers say they will not pay in English.

title: Culturally complete icon set and calendars
statement: Islamic icons, disability icons, Hijri and lunar calendars, bigger fonts — cheap, and in markets already blocked by localisation.

title: Billing must be exactly right
statement: Wrong amount, double charge, surprise renewal are the fastest route to 1★ (×21 lift); single price shown, no trial-to-charge traps, refunds honoured, receipts clear.

title: Sync must work — and prove it
statement: The paid feature that breaks most; sync failure is ×12.8 over-represented among buyers.

title: Crashes / launch failures
statement: Largest complaint by volume; a two-day launch crash produced more 1★ than years of minor bugs.

title: New Year peak-season robustness — year-end report and January onboarding
statement: The year-end report crashed five New Years in six; never ship risk or lock features in late December. The New Year cohort is the largest of the year and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day defect is amplified ~2× in January (reports 8, 9). The New Year cohort is the largest of the year and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day defect is amplified ~2× in January (reports 8, 9).

merged_from.title: Harden onboarding before January
merged_from.note: C146 (harden onboarding before January) is the same rule as C032 (never ship risk into late December) on a different surface

title: Restore purchase and entitlements must work immediately
statement: Charging and not delivering is the second-fastest route to 1★ (×13.9). Lifetime buyers told to subscribe, subscribers who cannot find their tier, premium members still upsold. Report 11: 3 of 3 paid reviewers lost purchased access — a lifetime non-consumable expired, a subscription re-locked after a week and reinstall did not restore, an active annual term was re-charged — and two titled their reviews 'scam' and 'Purchase fraud'.

title: Data must never be lost on update, reinstall or phone change
statement: Data loss is ×10.6 over-represented among buyers; local-only storage is the cause. Report 10: from 2025 the dominant story became app-initiated — 'it told me my pet data got corrupted' — with no automatic backup to fall back on.

title: Account system from day one
statement: Root cause of lost purchases, lost data and failed sync; requests rise as users change phones.

title: A support channel that exists, is reachable outside the app, and answers
statement: 'No support channel' is ×34.7 over-represented among buyers and the second-worst-rated complaint. Report 5: the only support link was inside an app that would not launch; email went unanswered while public review replies were same-day. Report 10: AI and canned support replies; paying users 13× over-represented among support complaints. Report 11: 'there is no way in app to talk with developer or team' — with no support queue, billing bugs were filed as public 1★ fraud accusations instead.

title: Family plan
statement: Demand exists (people bought it); report 1's failed only through discoverability (Apple Family Sharing with no in-app affordance).

title: Dates, streaks and statistics correct on every surface (incl. DST / timezone)
statement: Miscounts are ×10.2 over-represented among buyers. Off-by-one dates across app/widget/Watch were report 2's longest-lived bug. Night routines that cross midnight must log to the day they started, honouring a user 'day ends at' setting.

title: Reminders fire reliably, once
statement: Reminders that work are a top praise item; not firing or spamming is a 1★ driver.

title: Widgets must not go blank, stale or disagree with the app
statement: Broken widget is ×7.8 on 2★. Report 10: the widget rendered as a grey box for five years (117 reviews) — reported mostly by fans, so it never generated pressure.

title: Editing a habit never wipes its history
statement: Multi-year bug; fixing it brought reviewers back to raise their rating.

title: Aim at ADHD / neurodivergent users, students, medication & chronic-illness trackers
statement: Highest-fit, highest-satisfaction audiences (ADHD 7% of US at 4.79; students 4.87). Report 10: 7.36% of 70,041 reviewers self-identify as ADHD/autistic/ND; Australia's base is 11.4%.

title: Flexible / custom frequency
statement: Every X days, specific weekdays, bi-weekly, quarterly, yearly, total-over-a-window — the #1 unmet functional need and highest 4★ lift.

title: Mac / desktop / web app
statement: Strongest 3★ driver; users volunteer to pay extra for it.

title: Grouping / folders / categories / tags
statement: #2 feature request in report 1; the highest-mean request in report 3 (zero 1–2★, power users tracking 20–100 counters); named in report 8's only subscription-price statement.

title: Shortcuts / Siri / URL scheme / API
statement: Power users who evangelise.

title: Cumulative totals and total-days counter
statement: '47 hours read this year'; total days instead of consecutive to reduce streak anxiety.

title: Flexible units / partial progress
statement: Drag to 60% instead of a binary tick — a named reason for choosing over competitors.

title: Mood tracker
statement: Meaningful praise where shipped; mentions rose after launch (report 1); asked for only by 5★ users (report 8); an automatic mood prompt is a memory aid and moving it behind a button destroyed users' mood datasets (report 10).

title: One-off to-dos alongside habits
statement: Emerging request.

title: Android version
statement: Requested; cross-platform continuity matters to switchers.

title: Points / rewards / wish list
statement: Weak request; one proposes a cash-stake mode.

title: Custom time-of-day segments
statement: Beyond morning/afternoon/evening — shift workers.

title: Never run incentivised / review-for-premium campaigns
statement: Bought rank and a fake average, 0.86% purchase signal, reputational backlash, unreadable data.

title: Never gate or delete reviews
statement: Users catch it and call it a ToS violation.

title: Don't build AI features on demand grounds
statement: 0.011% demand; users ask for the opposite.

title: Offer a non-pastel / premium design option
statement: Recurring critique from men and users wanting a premium look.

title: Discovery runs through social video, Reddit, therapists (US) and Xiaohongshu / Bilibili (CN)
statement: Plan marketing around where users say they found the app. Report 10: 381 reviews involve a clinician recommending the app; two clinicians publicly withdrew the recommendation over data loss.

title: Be visibly responsive; fixes bring reviewers back
statement: Users who see their bug fixed return to raise their rating.

title: Cross-sell an app family on brand trust
statement: Under-used monetization asset.

title: Goodwill conversion — a generous free tier and 'support the devs'
statement: Small, pure-margin, mean 4.69. Report 5: the dominant purchase path was years of free use followed by upgrading to scale it or to say thanks.

title: Weight English-speaking rich markets; volume ≠ revenue
statement: Purchase-signal density is 8.5× higher in the US than China; BR/MX/ES/FR volume is localisation-blocked.

title: Free trial before purchase
statement: Weak but present complaint. Report 9: no trial in most storefronts drew 52 explicit requests, several saying they would have bought — and a trial offered in the US but not Saudi Arabia was compared in public.

title: Price level — where 'fair' turns into 'too expensive'
statement: Both coexist for one price; split follows market, payment rails and year.

title: Paying customers are the highest 1★ risk — every paid feature must work
statement: Paid cohort rates a full point lower; 28% of payers leave 1–2★; confirmed buyers ×6.7 on 1★. Report 10: paid-cohort mean fell 4.40 → 2.96 across 2022–2026 while the corpus mean barely moved; the five highest paid lifts are all billing mechanics, not price.

title: Focus timer
statement: Meaningful in the US, emerging globally.

title: Fitness / health tracking use case
statement: Very strong US use case.

title: Parents tracking kids
statement: Distinct use case; ties to profiles.

title: Check-off sound and haptic
statement: Named as a reason to keep coming back.

title: Use the language users use: Atomic Habits, 75 Hard
statement: Framing seen in US reviews.

title: Never ship and walk away
statement: Abandonment is visible to users within a year; the app becomes an OS-release liability for paying users with no recourse, while the store rating quietly rises on survivorship. Report 8: a ~18-month pause let iOS updates break the create flow, widget and launch, and users publicly asked whether the app was abandoned ('Wrapped 2022' still in settings in 2025).

title: Writes to shared system stores (calendar, health) must be exact and reversible
statement: A paid calendar sync that corrupts the user's calendar is the most severe complaint class in report 2.

title: Manual reordering, renaming and editing of habits/tasks — free
statement: Trivial, requested for years by 5★ users; best effort-to-goodwill ratio. In report 4 rename/reorder was gated and it was the top complaint among paying users.

title: Customisable, louder reminder sounds
statement: Asked by happy users; the cheapest 5★ upgrade.

title: Skippable, replayable onboarding tour
statement: Hidden gestures (swipe-to-complete, mode toggles) confuse new users; a US-specific 6% complaint in report 2.

title: Never seed launch reviews
statement: Users spot it in week one and say so; it contaminates the analytics baseline permanently.

title: Purchase and signup flow must not leak buyers
statement: People who try to pay and cannot (errors, rejected emails, promos that fail to apply) leave 2–4★ and money on the table.

title: Ship the paid feature working before you sell it
statement: Paid features carry a higher reliability bar; selling broken sync/calendar/stats put payers a full star below free users.

title: Personal photos as habit icons
statement: Rare, loved, and no competitor in report 2's corpus offers it.

title: Colour themes / dark mode
statement: 'Only green' draws requests; cheap. Report 10: dark mode requested since 2022 as an accessibility need (migraine, light sensitivity).

title: Ads in the free tier
statement: A mild negative and a minor purchase reason in report 2; 'no ads' is the best-rated topic in report 1.

title: Performance must not degrade with habit count
statement: 5+ second taps for the most engaged (paying) users; lag is a churn cause on its own.

title: Address tracking / privacy visibly
statement: One unrebutted 1★: 'a whole lotta tracking going on by the developer'.

title: Never imply cross-app integration you don't have
statement: Sibling apps raised expectations of integration; the purchases it drove ended in 1★.

title: No rating-prompt or cross-promo spam, especially to payers
statement: Small but consistent complaint.

title: Promos, giveaways and gift codes must work exactly as advertised
statement: Inflate early sentiment; when the promo fails to apply it produces 2–3★ from would-be buyers. Report 5's '1+1' gift code could not be used by the buyer and expired in three months — six years of disputes. Report 9: an advertised 3-month money-back guarantee was not honoured (17 reviews); withdrawing the claim zeroed those complaints and halved refund complaints.

title: Destructive actions on widgets, quick surfaces and running routines need confirmation or undo
statement: An un-undoable reset button on a Home Screen widget destroyed streaks by mis-tap and read as 'a visual cue to break the streak' — a safety issue in a recovery app.

title: Regional pricing
statement: IN, TR, UA, BR, MX, SA reviewers name price as the only blocker; India likes the product and has not yet been asked a price it can accept.

title: No upsell nagging without a 'never ask again' option
statement: Full-screen interstitials, permanent banners and upsells before first value draw complaints even from 5★ users; a subscription launch with nagging cost ~3 points of 1–2★. Report 9: upsell-pressure complaints quintupled (2.16% → 4.84% → 10.23%) as the funnel was tuned harder, becoming the fastest-growing 1★ source.

title: Ask for reviews well — tone converts; cadence and ignoring the OS opt-out backfire
statement: A charming review request produced dozens of reviews; frequent prompts that ignore the iOS opt-out, especially to payers, read as 'scammy'. Cross-promoting the developer's other apps inside the product draws the same complaint (report 2). Cross-promoting the developer's other apps inside the product draws the same complaint (report 2).

merged_from.title: No rating-prompt or cross-promo spam, especially to payers
merged_from.note: rating-prompt spam to payers was already the negative half of C094; cross-promo spam folded in

title: Neutral, non-judgemental tone on failure
statement: Reset without shame, no motivational pop-ups, keep history — the differentiation against apps that 'talk'.

title: Privacy and discretion stack
statement: Face ID / passcode lock, no account, discreet app name, alternate icons — zero negative reviews in report 3 and category-critical for recovery users on family phones.

title: A tip / donate option
statement: People asking to give money with no mechanism to do so. Report 8: in a completely free app, 7 users asked unprompted for a tip jar (all 5★) and 13 more volunteered to pay — mostly one-time, not subscription.

title: Time-unit flexibility for counters (hours → years)
statement: What makes day 1 survivable for a quit-habit user; zero 1–2★.

title: Countdown / 'days until' mode
statement: Users want one app for count-up and count-down.

title: Money-saved counter
statement: Standard in quit-smoking apps; named as the one thing missing.

title: Milestones, achievements, celebration
statement: The largest positive-intent request in report 3 (2.21%, six years); shipped Aug 2026.

title: Inverse / 'good habit' mode for a counter
statement: Recovery users want the number up; chore/ADHD users want it low — one counter, two mental models.

title: Vulnerable users — recovery, mental-health and minors — are a sensitive surface
statement: Alcohol, nicotine, self-harm (incl. minors), drugs, EDs, no-contact; monetisation moves land as 'preying on the vulnerable'; age rating is load-bearing. In report 4: 455 kid/teen reviews who cannot pay, and 89 shame / diet-framing reviews in a 4+ app.

title: Never ship a paywall or feature-removal change silently
statement: Undisclosed changes and 'it was a bug' replies that don't match what users see destroy trust for a year. Report 11: the store description still discloses no paywall at all (0 mentions of premium/subscription/free/unlock) after the retrofit; a grandfathering rule for pre-2026 users is the recommended fix.

title: Widget variants and customisation as the paid layer
statement: Base single-counter widget free forever; multi-counter widgets, custom art, progress rings, reset-from-widget can be paid — and were report 3's #1 purchase trigger.

title: Goals / targets
statement: Tolerated behind the paywall (mean 4.05) and a stated purchase reason.

title: A free trial must be a real trial
statement: It must apply to whichever plan the user picks, and the confirmation must show the exact charge date and amount; a trial that bills at once produced 789 reviews at mean 1.35 in report 4 and must be verified per storefront (Brazil ran 7–11× the global rate). Report 10: 149 users believe they were charged at trial START (mean 1.79) and trial length varied between 2 and 7 days across users.

title: An obvious 'continue free' path on the paywall — the free/paid boundary must be legible
statement: Users wrote 75 reviews teaching each other where the hidden X was while 1,903 said the app was paid-only; legibility of what is free is a rating decision.

title: No long quiz before the price; show the price up front
statement: A 10–20 minute quiz followed by a paywall turns a price objection into anger (mean 1.98, 71.9% 1–2★); 'lower the yearly price a bit and show it at the very beginning'.

title: In-app cancellation
statement: Cancel-by-email with no reply converts recoverable disputes into permanent 1★, legal threats and denied refunds.

title: One stable, disclosed price — no discount wheels
statement: Users in the same market reported $19.99–$59.99 for the same thing; that inconsistency is what 'scam' language attaches to; a rigged or broken gimmick makes it worse. Report 10: household members quoted $34.99 vs $41.99 on the same day, support could not explain a $19.99–$99.99 range — perceived as discriminatory pricing inside families.

title: Ads must match the app
statement: Advertised features that are absent create a 'scam' cohort before first open (0.62%, mean 2.42).

title: Content library (workouts, meditation, sleep, journal) as the paid layer
statement: Gives a routine app something to sell beyond the core loop and separates it from 'a fancy Reminders list'.

title: Mascot / companion character
statement: Small, pure praise in report 4; category norm in pet-style apps. Report 10: the pet is the causal story users tell — 'I will do for the bird what I will not do for myself' — at 70,041-review scale (companion 1,309, cute design 10,074); the same attachment makes data loss feel like bereavement.

title: Preset routines / templates / programs
statement: Paywalled in report 4 with little complaint.

title: Redesigns must not regress layout — ship a density / text-size option or an opt-out
statement: A compact-list redesign produced a dated backlash (report 7) while a Liquid Glass refresh drew none (report 8); layout regressions hit neurodivergent users hardest (report 4); a Feb 2024 redesign and continuous UI churn drew a backlash cluster (report 10).

title: Sequential routine timer with spoken next step and live finish-time estimate
statement: Report 5's product thesis: removes the need to hold a schedule in working memory and says continuously whether you are still on time; 162 reviewers report they stopped being late. The voice needs an off switch.

title: Untimed / checklist mode as a per-routine toggle
statement: A real minority of the ADHD audience finds a mandatory timer anxiety-inducing; the fix is an option per routine, not a separate object.

title: Background battery and thermals
statement: A background timer that drains 30–90% of daily battery and heats the device is report 5's worst non-billing theme (mean 2.94) and loses subscribers who otherwise love the app.

title: Notification escalation must be user-configurable, never silently retuned
statement: Some users depend on an un-dismissable alarm, others are driven out by it; a global default serves both badly; removing it broke wake-ups for loyal subscribers.

title: Never show ads to paying subscribers
statement: Including reward-gated features like streak savers; a 30-second unskippable ad to a payer is the most reliable way to turn an advocate into a 1★. Report 10: a sponsored movie tie-in as the monthly event drew 'I am paying to be advertised to' from multi-year subscribers (mean 3.09, 8× over-represented among payers) after 857 reviews had praised the app for being ad-free.

title: Use the lead-user market as the beta cohort
statement: Report 5's home market (Korea) carries the deepest engineering feedback and most detailed feature specs — and uses the review page as a support desk.

title: No default-on social feed in a personal tool
statement: Unwanted by a vocal minority, and a child-safety liability when minors and adults share a feed on a 17+ app.

title: Do not sell in a storefront where the app cannot function
statement: Seven years of 'will not open' from mainland China, with users charged for an app that shows 'no network'. Report 9: in Russia 46% of reviews say the app loads for minutes or only works over a VPN, while 32% of Russian reviewers had paid.

title: Gate on capability, not on quantity
statement: A quantity cap set above the point of core value is noticed, tolerated and does not convert; move the wall to analytics, sync, Watch, widgets, icons, family sharing. See Research Reports/Feature Gating vs Quantity.md. Report 6 contests the 'icons' part: the listing sold Premium on themes and icons and zero of 44 reviewers mentioned them.

title: Lead the store listing with what users actually love
statement: Report 6's most-loved feature (the free widget) was one bullet at the bottom of the description and its differentiators (no daily check-in, user-defined day boundary) were not marketed at all — yet they are why people switched.

title: Offer both check-in tracking and auto-counting (no daily check-in) per item
statement: A counter that runs on its own until you declare a break is report 6's differentiator against every check-off tracker, and fits abstinence streaks best.

title: When an item can be tracked more than one way, make the user choose the mode at creation
statement: Report 6: users who landed in the auto-count mode by default read it as the app fabricating progress (1★), and users asked for a mode that already shipped.

title: Show the paywall at the moment of need, not on app open
statement: Surface the upgrade when the user tries the gated action (the third streak, a freeze); an upsell on every launch reads as 'begs me for money' and feeds the greed cluster.

title: Never let the paywall imply a capability the product lacks
statement: A buyer who paid for a feature that isn't there cancels and says 'there are free ones'; it turns a feature request into a refund cause.

title: Cache entitlements locally — never block a paid surface on a live server check
statement: Report 7: widgets that re-checked Pro against a network service showed 'Upgrade' to paying users for 15 months (100% payers, mean 2.25), 4× more often in markets with VPN/DNS filtering; render from the last-known-good receipt.

title: Market the generic-tracker use case
statement: Report 7: users track medication, migraines, supplements for a pet, art-project days — any yes/no daily thing — at mean 4.91, while the listing only says 'build habits'.

title: Native iPad layout
statement: A stretched phone UI on iPad does more rating damage than a missing Watch app and is cheaper to fix — a layout, not a new product (report 7).

title: Surface existing features where users look
statement: Features hidden behind 'Advanced Options' or unexplained modes are rated as missing — including by payers who bought and then believed the feature absent; report 7's weekly goals, multi-habit widget and notifications.

title: Intra-day completion: tap N times to fill N/N
statement: When a habit's target is more than once a day, each tap should count toward it; one binary tick per day is report 8's #1 unmet need, the only complaint theme still rising, and a stated uninstall.

title: Habits, focus timer and journal in one simple app
statement: Report 8's 3-in-1 bundle is load-bearing: none of the three parts draws a 1–2★, and users value not switching between three apps — as long as each part stays minimal.

title: Every promotional or onboarding modal must be dismissible on the smallest screen
statement: Report 8's full-screen 'add a widget' prompt had an unreachable close button on small iPhones and blocked the app for 20 months.

title: Harden onboarding before January
statement: The New Year cohort is the largest of the year, writes reviews in its first days, and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day logging defect is amplified about 2× in January (report 8).

title: Let people use the product before they pay
statement: Users forgive a price; they do not forgive paying blind. Report 9's hard paywall before any experience produced 159 'let me look before you charge me' reviews at mean 1.79, and buyers who paid before seeing the product became the angriest cohort (mean 1.94).

title: The paid product must deliver what the ads and onboarding demonstrate
statement: Report 9 showed an interactive guided-breathing coach in its ads and onboarding, then never offered it again — 'it's just a checklist' became the worst-rated major theme (99 reviews, mean 1.45), half of them from payers.

title: Respect Reduce Motion — no rapid flashing animation
statement: A self-care app's fast animation was reported as a seizure/vertigo risk (report 9, promoted as a safety finding despite one review).

title: Never ask for a rating before the user has used the app
statement: Report 9 put the rating prompt inside sign-up: users were asked for 5★ before seeing the app, the public rating ran 1.35 stars above written reviews, and Apple's guidelines forbid it.

title: Never cap or paywall a support conversation mid-crisis
statement: Report 9's AI coach hit its free message cap while a user was 'almost having a collapse'; an emotional-support chat needs an uncapped crisis path and a handoff to real help.

title: A promised pre-charge trial reminder must actually arrive — in-app, with amount and date
statement: Report 10: 'you promised to remind me before charging' is the highest-intensity complaint in a 70,041-review corpus (billing-dispute family mean 1.97, 60% one-star, 17% of all payers); the reminder must be a blocking in-app card on next open, not only a push, and the exact amount and charge date must sit on the trial screen and permanently in Settings. For an ADHD audience the reminder is the feature, not a courtesy.

title: Automatic cloud backup on by default — never manual opt-in
statement: Report 10: progress stored on-device with a manual opt-in backup produced 551 data-loss reviews (9% of all 1★), a family rate that quadrupled in four years, and clinicians publicly withdrawing recommendations; 37 users did not know a backup was required until after the loss. Warn before any destructive path (delete for storage, phone change).

title: Compensation for lost data must match the loss — never a flat token
statement: Report 10: a flat 5,000-stone remedy offered to users who lost 20,000–200,000 stones, multi-year streaks and unrepeatable items was described as insulting and in bereavement language; restore inventory or history, not a token.

title: Never remove a feature people bought the app for — add alongside, do not replace
statement: Report 10: every major removal (Journeys → streak-based Self-Care Areas, automatic mood check-ins, exact-time goals, milestones, colour palettes) produced a dated backlash, explicit paid cancellations, and none were reversed; generic 'you removed a feature I used' grew 16× in four years.

title: Content and event releases need a crash gate across device generations
statement: Report 10: a monthly event's 'grow potion' animation crashed the app on load for a large cohort (120 crash reviews in Feb 2026, 4–6× baseline), destroying 600-day streaks and locking paid users out for weeks; reviewers blame the event cadence for shipping untested code.

title: Every guilt mechanic must be optional — streaks, repair prompts, countdowns
statement: Report 10: the app was praised specifically for not guilting users (476 reviews, mean 4.87); after streaks shipped mid-2024, 96 reviews say it now punishes the missed day the audience was promised it wouldn't, and repairing a streak costs currency. A single 'gentle mode' toggle is the corpus's own proposal.

title: Credit for non-consecutive, cumulative progress alongside streaks
statement: Report 10: replacing cumulative Journeys with consecutive-streak Self-Care Areas was the lowest-rated change in the corpus (mean 2.76, 21 of 49 one-star); chronic-illness and ADHD users say a streak-only model is structurally incompatible with their lives. Ship cumulative credit next to streaks, not instead of them.

title: Launch-to-core-action path with no interstitials
statement: Report 10: 'overwhelm' is the largest UX complaint (1,046 reviews) — an app sold to people with executive-function difficulty accumulated six sequential screens (quote, mood prompt, event cutscene, visitor, chest, claim-confirm-claim) before the checklist.

title: Honour what onboarding asks — a declared limitation must change the suggestions
statement: Report 10: the onboarding asks about disability and then ignores the answer ('I have mobility issues, so I clicked that… ever since, the app has been suggesting that I do things that I've told it I can't do'); 597 accessibility reviews at mean 4.56.

title: Values and identity screens are optional in both directions
statement: Report 10: 54 users deleted at a mandatory pet-pronoun step, 109 objected to Pride content, and 111 loyal users (mean 4.57) complained representation was missing; the only intervention the corpus supports is a skip option and a show/hide filter for themed cosmetics — optionality, not editorial change.

title: Automated suggestions from user text must be safety-filtered; notifications must be crisis-aware
statement: Report 10: the goal-suggestion system parsed a journal entry about suicidal ideation into a goal to 'schedule time for suicide'; diagnosis quizzes returned severe results to children in a 4+ app; a 'you can do this' push arrived right after a text about suicide.

title: Visible monthly plan — annual-default trials drive billing disputes
statement: Report 10: the 7-day trial defaults to an annual charge; 23 reviews ask for a monthly plan and several say they would have paid monthly; the annual default is the mechanism behind most of the 404 billing disputes.

title: A random-rotation shop with paid re-rolls and unpurchasable catalogue items is a friction generator
statement: Report 10: goals yield 3–12 stones while items cost 500–900, the shop rotates randomly, and the item you want never appears — 196 complaints from engaged, currency-rich users, the ones most likely to subscribe. Let users buy what they can see.

title: Official community channels must tolerate criticism
statement: Report 10: the Facebook group, Discord and subreddit are described as heavily moderated and hostile to criticism across five years (211 reviews), with paying users 7× over-represented; suppression of criticism resurfaces in every later controversy.

title: Keep the therapeutic core in front of the game layer
statement: Report 10: as breathing, first aid and soundscapes moved behind menus and paywalls, tool mentions fell 15.6% → 2.7% and the core-benefit family 30% → 23%, while reviewers called the product 'a pay-to-play loot box checklist simulator'; the game is why people call it cute and motivating, but it must not be paid for by burying the layer people came for.

title: Cosmetic and colour variety as the paid layer
statement: Report 10: buyers name extra colour options, seasonal items and a larger shop as the specific hook ('I started getting finch plus solely because I found the extra color options… very motivating'); restricting palettes later (Aug–Sep 2026) drew a backlash.

title: Monthly seasonal event with a paid reward track
statement: Report 10: event completion is a stated purchase trigger, but events are also the named cause of the 2026 crash and data-loss clusters, FOMO complaints, and the sponsored-IP values breach.

title: Completion verification / anti-cheat
statement: Report 10: 158 users volunteer that they check boxes without doing the task and ask to be held accountable (mean 4.59); its sibling 'it's just a checklist' (111) is the churn thesis.

title: Configurable day boundary and hemisphere seasons
statement: Report 10: 146 reviews say the app assumes a conventional daytime schedule and northern-hemisphere seasons; night-shift workers and southern-hemisphere users ask for a movable day boundary.

title: Accessibility stack: VoiceOver, motion, sound and light sensitivity, text size
statement: Report 10: 597 accessibility reviews (0.85%, mean 4.56) from blind, mobility-limited, chronically ill, motion-, sound- and light-sensitive users; dark mode is argued as an accessibility need, not a preference ('Cute clothes for the bird were apparently shippable').

title: Per-day / per-habit notes and journal text
statement: A note field on each check-in is pure upside and requested by happy users (reports 2, 3, 7); a single cramped line is the common complaint; charging for journal text while mood is free drew complaints (report 9).

title: Sub-tasks / sub-routines nested inside a habit or routine
statement: 'Shower routine' reused inside 'morning routine'; sub-habits are what heavy users ask for after categories (reports 1, 5, 7).

title: Multiple profiles (me, kids, pet, work)
statement: Requested alongside folders in report 1 — separate people or contexts inside one app.

title: Updates must not break function or wipe progress
statement: 'Then Boom… updated! Now… the progress is gone' (report 4); a nine-week window of hard functional failures (report 8); an update broke chronological sorting across four countries in one week (report 9); near-daily forced updates are themselves a complaint (report 10).

title: Never let fear of losing history be the reason people pay
statement: Report 11: the only stated purchase motive was 'I had 3 years worth of history I didn't want to lose' on an app with no export or backup; when the entitlement then failed, the loyal long-tenure user became the 1★ 'scam' review. Sell durability (backup, export, long-history analytics) as a gain, never gate access to what the user already built.

title: Every IAP SKU has a distinct name that states its period or 'one time'
statement: Report 11: three SKUs shared the identical display name 'Habits PRO Functions' at $1.99 / $6.99 / $8.99 and none named a period, while reviewers described 'annual', 'VIP' and 'lifetime' purchases — neither the user nor support could tell what had been bought.

title: A quiet, adult, non-gamified tracker is a positioning some users actively seek
statement: Report 11: 'Functional, no frills and no infantilization. I tested half a dozen similar apps before finding this one'; 'I hate apps that demand set times'; 'without any imposed junk' — four of 33 reviewers chose the app for what it refuses to do, and three switched from gamified competitors. A live tension with the pet/mascot category norm.

title: Do not run a paid twin app beside the free app
statement: Report 11: a separate 'Lifetime Premium' binary collected one rating in six years, ran a version behind, undercut the in-app lifetime SKU by $5 and created a second entitlement surface that plausibly fed the 'lifetime subscription… suddenly cancelled' confusion.
